instructions: If creating a new Word document, first read the entire docx-js.md file completely from start to finish without setting any range limits, then create a JavaScript/TypeScript file using Document, Paragraph, and TextRun components, and export as .docx using Packer.toBuffer()
If editing an existing Word document, first read the entire ooxml.md file completely from start to finish without setting any range limits
Unpack the document using the command: python ooxml/scripts/unpack.py <office_file> <output_directory>
Create and run a Python script using the Document library to make edits
Pack the final document using the command: python ooxml/scripts/pack.py <input_directory> <office_file>
If editing someone else's document, a legal, academic, business, or government document, or when in doubt, use the Redlining workflow
In the Redlining workflow, convert the document to markdown with tracked changes preserved using the command: pandoc --track-changes=all path-to-file.docx -o current.md
In the Redlining workflow, identify all changes needed and organize them into logical batches of 3-10 related changes
In the Redlining workflow, locate changes using section/heading numbers, paragraph identifiers, grep patterns with unique surrounding text, or document structure, but do not use markdown line numbers

In the Redlining workflow, read the entire ooxml.md file completely from start to finish without setting any range limits, paying special attention to the Document Library and Tracked Change Patterns sections
In the Redlining workflow, unpack the document using the command: python ooxml/scripts/unpack.py <file.docx> <dir>
In the Redlining workflow, note the suggested RSID provided by the unpack script and use it for tracked changes
In the Redlining workflow, implement changes in batches of 3-10 related changes, grouping them by section, type, complexity, or sequential order
For each batch, grep for text in word/document.xml to verify how text is split across <w:r> elements
For each batch, use get_node to find nodes, implement changes, then call doc.save()
Always grep word/document.xml immediately before writing a script to get current line numbers and verify text content
When implementing tracked changes, only mark text that actually changes, breaking replacements into unchanged text plus deletion plus insertion plus unchanged text
When implementing tracked changes, preserve the original run's RSID for unchanged text by extracting the <w:r> element from the original and reusing it
After all batches are complete, pack the document using the command: python ooxml/scripts/pack.py unpacked reviewed-document.docx
Perform final verification by converting the final document to markdown using the command: pandoc --track-changes=all reviewed-document.docx -o verification.md
Verify all changes were applied correctly by grepping for original phrases (should not find them) and replacement phrases (should find them) in verification.md
Check that no unintended changes were introduced in the final document
If needing to read text contents of a document, convert the document to markdown using pandoc with the command: pandoc --track-changes=all path-to-file.docx -o output.md

If needing raw XML access for comments, complex formatting, document structure, embedded media, or metadata, unpack the document using the command: python ooxml/scripts/unpack.py <office_file> <output_directory>
To visually analyze Word documents, convert DOCX to PDF using the command: soffice --headless --convert-to pdf document.docx
To visually analyze Word documents, convert PDF pages to JPEG images using the command: pdftoppm -jpeg -r 150 document.pdf page
When generating code for DOCX operations, write concise code, avoid verbose variable names and redundant operations, and avoid unnecessary print statements

Install required dependencies if not available: pandoc via sudo apt-get install pandoc, docx via npm install -g docx, LibreOffice via sudo apt-get install libreoffice, Poppler via sudo apt-get install poppler-utils, and defusedxml via pip install defusedxml
